context.title: Jacob Steals the Blessing
context.summary: As blind, aging Isaac prepares to bless Esau, Rebekah helps Jacob disguise himself in goat skins and take the blessing; Esau weeps for a blessing of his own and vows to kill Jacob, and Rebekah sends Jacob away.
context.background: A father's final blessing was understood as binding, like a spoken will; once given, it could not be taken back (vv. 33, 37). Blind Isaac relies on touch, smell, taste and hearing, and each is deceived.

customs.note: The blessing passed on headship of the family. Isaac's words include rule over his brothers and an echo of God's promise to Abraham (12:3).

watchFor: 'The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau' (v. 22).
Goat skins deceive a father here; a goat's blood will deceive Jacob in 37:31.

w: and he bore a grudge against

people.name: Esau
people.summary: Hairy, Rebekah’s first-born twin son (Gen. 25:25). The name of Edom, “red”, was also given to him from his conduct in connection with the red lentil “pottage” for which he sold his birthright (30, 31).

people.name: Isaac
people.summary: The only son of Abraham by Sarah. He was the longest lived of the three patriarchs (Gen. 21:1-3).

people.name: Rebekah
people.summary: A noose, the daughter of Bethuel, and the wife of Isaac (Gen. 22:23; 24:67). The circumstances under which Abraham’s “steward” found her at the “city of Nahor,” in Padan-aram, are narrated in Gen. 24-27.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

people.name: Laban
people.summary: The son of Bethuel, who was the son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother. He lived at Haran in Mesopotamia. His sister Rebekah was Isaac’s wife (Gen. 24).

people.name: Heth
people.summary: Dread, a descendant of Canaan, and the ancestor of the Hittites (Gen. 10:18; Deut. 7:1), who dwelt in the vicinity of Hebron (Gen. 23:3, 7).

places.name: Haran
places.summary: Heb. haran, i.e., “parched;” or probably from the Accadian charana, meaning “a road.” A celebrated city of Western Asia, now Harran, where Abram remained, after he left Ur of the Chaldees, till his father Terah died (Gen. 11:31, 32), when he continued his journey into the land of Canaan.
